expectations.text: Identifies that during the rollout window old code runs against the new schema
expectations.evidence: "For a few minutes, old pods are still running the old code that reads legacy_email, against a schema where the column is gone. That window is the outage."

expectations.text: Recommends splitting into separate deploys (expand/contract) rather than shipping the drop with the code
expectations.evidence: "Today: merge and deploy only the three code changes... Later, Monday-ish: a separate PR containing only the DROP."

expectations.text: States that dropping the column is irreversible without a backup or restore
expectations.evidence: "Rolling back the deploy rolls back the code; it does not bring the column back. Your only restore path is a point-in-time restore of the database."

expectations.text: Addresses what rollback looks like if the deploy goes wrong
expectations.evidence: "Code-only deploy: rollback is a revert, minutes, safe alone at 5pm. Post-DROP: rollback is a database restore with someone paged on a weekend."

expectations.text: Addresses the Friday timing in terms of who is available to respond, not as superstition
expectations.evidence: "Post-DROP: rollback is a database restore with someone paged on a weekend."

expectations.text: Recommends a CI gate that blocks destructive DDL from landing alongside application code
expectations.evidence: "a CI check that fails when a migration file containing DROP/destructive ALTER lands in the same PR as application code."

expectations.text: Does not approve the merge as-is on the strength of green CI
expectations.evidence: "merge and deploy only the three code changes... hold the DROP."

expectations.text: Distinguishes the reversible parts of the change from the irreversible part
expectations.evidence: "Fully reversible — revert reverts it" vs the DROP which is not reversible.
